title: "Finding noun chunks from grammar links"
subtitle: "Compare spaCy phrases with small dependency chunks"
description: "Learn how noun chunks group nouns with attached words, using spaCy and a local UDPipe dependency parse."
categories: [phrases and entities, noun chunks, workforce research]

After counting adjacent phrases, the Riverton Workforce Lab must choose its
units for checks. It considers `basic spreadsheet skills` as one phrase or three
separate words.

A grammar-aware method offers one convention for making that choice. It can
group candidate phrases for checks, but it does not create a single correct
inventory of English phrases.

::: {.callout-note}
The author created the fictional Riverton Workforce Lab, its job board, and
its training flyer for teaching.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn

Use this lesson to practice how to:

- describe a noun chunk in plain language.
- extract noun chunks with a trained spaCy pipeline.
- build simple chunks from a UDPipe dependency parse.
- explain why chunk definitions differ across tools.
- separate agreement from accuracy.
- explain why parser errors affect chunk rules.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

options(warn = 2)
stopifnot(identical(getOption("warn"), 2L))
```

## Ask a trained pipeline for noun chunks

The setup reads the text file and runs spaCy.
It also prepares inputs for a small UDPipe-based rule.
A **noun chunk** is a short, nonnested phrase around one noun.
It contains the noun and directly preceding determiners, numbers, compounds,
and describing words.

Under this convention, chunks neither nest nor extend past the noun.
Thus `evening classes in October` produces `evening classes` and `October`,
not one longer phrase. Tools can apply different boundary conventions.

```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(tokenizers)
library(udpipe)
library(spacyr)
source("R/use-spacy.R")

sentences <- read_csv(
  "data/workforce/workforce_sentences.csv",
  na = character(),
  col_types = cols(
    sentence_id = col_character(),
    document_id = col_character(),
    source_line = col_character(),
    text = col_character(),
    reference_label = col_character(),
    uncertainty = col_character(),
    annotator_id = col_character(),
    rationale = col_character(),
    codebook_version = col_character(),
    codebook_hash = col_character(),
    derived = col_character(),
    transformation = col_character()
  )
)

pipeline <- use_project_spacy()
pipeline_info <- spacy_pipeline_version()
parsed_spacy <- spacy_parse(
  setNames(sentences$text, sentences$sentence_id),
  pos = TRUE,
  lemma = TRUE,
  entity = TRUE,
  dependency = TRUE,
  nounphrase = TRUE
)
spacy_phrases <- nounphrase_extract(parsed_spacy) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(doc_id, chunk = str_replace_all(nounphrase, "_", " "))

example_text <- "Riverton Skills Centre will run evening classes in October."
example_parsed <- spacy_parse(
  c(example = example_text),
  pos = TRUE,
  lemma = TRUE,
  entity = TRUE,
  dependency = TRUE,
  nounphrase = TRUE
)
example_phrases <- nounphrase_extract(example_parsed) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(chunk = str_replace_all(nounphrase, "_", " "))

spacy_finalize()

pipeline_table <- tibble(
  field = names(pipeline_info),
  value = unlist(pipeline_info, use.names = FALSE)
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  pipeline_table,
  col.names = c("Pipeline field", "Value"),
  caption = "spaCy pipeline used for noun chunks",
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  spacy_phrases |>
    slice_head(n = 12),
  col.names = c("Sentence ID", "spaCy noun chunk"),
  caption = "First spaCy noun chunks from the Riverton text units",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(all(
  c("readr", "dplyr", "tibble", "purrr", "stringr", "tokenizers", "udpipe", "spacyr") %in%
    loadedNamespaces()
))

stopifnot(
  identical(nrow(sentences), 28L),
  identical(pipeline$model, "en_core_web_sm"),
  identical(pipeline_info$version, "3.8.0"),
  identical(pipeline_info$license, "MIT"),
  identical(pipeline_info$spacy, "3.8.7"),
  identical(nrow(parsed_spacy), 179L),
  identical(nrow(spacy_phrases), 40L),
  identical(spacy_phrases$chunk[spacy_phrases$doc_id == "s001"], "Paid 12-week training"),
  identical(spacy_phrases$chunk[spacy_phrases$doc_id == "s017"], "A valid driver's license"),
  identical(
    example_phrases$chunk,
    c("Riverton Skills Centre", "evening classes", "October")
  )
)
```

The released spaCy pipeline returns 40 noun chunks for the 28 text units. For the
check sentence, it returns three flat chunks: `Riverton Skills Centre`, `evening
classes`, and `October`.

## Build chunks from dependency links

The site's UDPipe model uses 500 training sentences.
Evaluation used 13 held-out political weblog posts from 2003 to 2006.
Unlabelled attachment was 0.7235, and labelled attachment was 0.6561.
spaCy's released production model uses far more training text.
This comparison illustrates different methods, not equivalent training
conditions.

The local UDPipe model has no tokenizer, so the lesson gives it one token per
line. In the code, `\(tokens)` is R shorthand for a small function that handles
one sentence's tokens at a time.

The classroom rule starts from each `NOUN` or `PROPN` token.
It collects direct dependents with these relations:

- `det` identifies determiners such as `a` or `the`.
- `amod` identifies describing words.
- `compound` links nouns within a compound.
- `nummod` identifies numbers that modify nouns.

```{r}
parser <- udpipe_load_model("data/treebank/en_ewt-500-parser.udpipe")

vertical <- sentences$text |>
  tokenize_words(lowercase = FALSE, strip_punct = FALSE) |>
  map_chr(\(tokens) paste(tokens, collapse = "\n"))

annotated <- udpipe_annotate(
  parser,
  x = vertical,
  doc_id = sentences$sentence_id,
  tokenizer = "vertical",
  tagger = "default",
  parser = "default"
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  as_tibble()

token_count_gap <- parsed_spacy |>
  count(doc_id, name = "spacy_tokens") |>
  inner_join(
    annotated |>
      count(doc_id, name = "udpipe_tokens"),
    by = "doc_id"
  ) |>
  filter(spacy_tokens != udpipe_tokens)

chunk_relations <- c("det", "amod", "compound", "nummod")

collect_chunk <- function(current_doc_id, current_token_id) {
  annotated |>
    filter(
      doc_id == current_doc_id,
      token_id == current_token_id |
        (head_token_id == current_token_id & dep_rel %in% chunk_relations)
    ) |>
    arrange(as.integer(token_id)) |>
    pull(token) |>
    str_c(collapse = " ")
}

udpipe_chunks <- annotated |>
  filter(upos %in% c("NOUN", "PROPN")) |>
  transmute(
    doc_id,
    token_id,
    chunk = map2_chr(doc_id, token_id, collect_chunk)
  ) |>
  select(doc_id, chunk)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  token_count_gap,
  col.names = c("Sentence ID", "spaCy tokens", "UDPipe tokens"),
  caption = "The one token-count difference between the two parses",
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  udpipe_chunks |>
    slice_head(n = 12),
  col.names = c("Sentence ID", "UDPipe-built chunk"),
  caption = "First noun chunks built from dependency links",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(nrow(annotated), 178L),
  identical(token_count_gap$doc_id, "s017"),
  identical(token_count_gap$spacy_tokens, 8L),
  identical(token_count_gap$udpipe_tokens, 7L),
  identical(nrow(udpipe_chunks), 56L),
  identical(udpipe_chunks$chunk[1:5], c("Paid", "Paid week", "week training", "No prior data experience", "Evening schedules")),
  identical(annotated$upos[annotated$doc_id == "s001" & annotated$token == "Paid"], "PROPN"),
  identical(udpipe_chunks$chunk[udpipe_chunks$doc_id == "s027"], "No prior experience")
)
```

Different tokenization produces different row counts.
In `s017`, spaCy separates `driver's` into `driver` and `'s`.
UDPipe's tokenizer retains one token, which explains the 179 versus 178 rows.
spaCy's displayed chunks still contain `Paid 12-week training` and
`A valid driver's license`. The difference concerns token rows, not those
chunk strings.

The rule emits one chunk for every noun-like tag, so chunks can overlap.
The chunks `Paid`, `Paid week`, and `week training` come from the same four
words in `s001`. The rule joins heads and dependents without an adjacency check.
Thus `Paid week` omits `12-` and does not occur in the source.

The chunk `Paid` results from an incorrect `PROPN` tag.
Here, `Paid` describes training. Chunk rules can propagate tagging errors and
introduce additional errors.

## Compare the two lists

Exact agreement is strict: the sentence ID and the chunk text must both match.
That makes agreement a string match, not accuracy. Neither list is ground truth,
and spaCy chunks are non-overlapping while the UDPipe-built list can overlap.

```{r}
agreed_chunks <- inner_join(
  distinct(spacy_phrases),
  distinct(udpipe_chunks),
  by = c("doc_id", "chunk")
)

comparison_summary <- tibble(
  measure = c("spaCy chunks", "UDPipe-built chunks", "exact agreements"),
  count = c(nrow(spacy_phrases), nrow(udpipe_chunks), nrow(agreed_chunks))
)

different_examples <- tibble(
  method = c("spaCy", "UDPipe-built"),
  sentence_id = c("s005", "s005"),
  chunk = c("A high school diploma", "A high school"),
  explanation = c(
    "spaCy keeps the full education phrase.",
    "The dependency rule attaches words to school and leaves diploma outside this chunk."
  )
)

spreadsheet_examples <- bind_rows(
  spacy_phrases |>
    filter(doc_id == "s004", str_detect(chunk, "spreadsheet")) |>
    mutate(method = "spaCy"),
  udpipe_chunks |>
    filter(doc_id == "s004", str_detect(chunk, "spreadsheet")) |>
    mutate(method = "UDPipe-built")
) |>
  select(method, doc_id, chunk)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  comparison_summary,
  col.names = c("Measure", "Count"),
  caption = "String matches across two chunking conventions",
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  different_examples,
  col.names = c("Method", "Sentence ID", "Chunk", "Explanation"),
  caption = "One sentence where the two chunk methods differ",
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  spreadsheet_examples,
  col.names = c("Method", "Sentence ID", "Chunk"),
  caption = "How each method handles the spreadsheet-skills phrase",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(nrow(spacy_phrases), 40L),
  identical(nrow(udpipe_chunks), 56L),
  identical(nrow(agreed_chunks), 25L),
  identical(spacy_phrases$chunk[spacy_phrases$doc_id == "s005"], "A high school diploma"),
  identical(udpipe_chunks$chunk[udpipe_chunks$doc_id == "s005"], "A high school"),
  identical(agreed_chunks$chunk[1], "No prior data experience"),
  identical(
    spreadsheet_examples$chunk,
    c("basic spreadsheet skills", "spreadsheet", "need basic spreadsheet skills")
  )
)
```

The lists have 25 exact string matches, which measure agreement, not accuracy.
The counts 40 and 56 describe different chunk definitions.
spaCy groups `basic spreadsheet skills`.
The UDPipe rule also emits `spreadsheet` and incorrectly includes `need` in
`need basic spreadsheet skills`.

A bigram groups adjacent words even across phrase boundaries.
A dependency chunk groups words according to parser links.
Its usefulness depends on correct parsing.

## What to remember

- Noun chunks are flat, non-overlapping spans under a tool-specific convention.
- spaCy returns 40 noun chunks for these 28 text units.
- The UDPipe-built rule returns 56 overlapping chunks from a deliberately weak teaching model.
- The 25 exact matches are agreement, not accuracy.
- `Paid week` shows how a rule can manufacture text by pasting non-adjacent tokens.
- Tokenization alone explains the 179 versus 178 row-count gap.

Use chunk lists to select text for human checks.
When tools disagree, examine the source, tokenization, and parse before
interpreting the phrase.
